[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-I18N-002-medicaid-portal-localization.md#decision-summary]

## Decision Summary

Portal Studio uses a two-layer i18n architecture. The Studio UI uses `next-intl` with static message catalogs. Portal content uses a bake-at-publish model — all translated strings are compiled into the Page Assembly artifact at publish time and resolved client-side with zero round-trips on locale switch. Default locales are `en-US` (source, non-removable) and `es-MX` for all portals and Product Packages. All user-visible strings must be 100% localized — no hard-coded strings are permitted. Machine translation (MT) via the Gainwell AI Agentic Framework provides the 100% coverage baseline; human post-editing promotes strings to human-translated (HTR) status.

---
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-I18N-002-medicaid-portal-localization.md#context-and-problem-statement]

## Context and Problem Statement

**Business Context:** Medicaid portals serve linguistically diverse populations. Spanish (`es-MX`) is a baseline requirement for all portals. Translation at scale requires MT with human post-editing (MTPE) rather than full human translation.

**Technical Context:** The system has two distinct i18n surfaces: the Studio UI (for the implementation team) and portal content (for end users). Portal content must be fully localized in every registered target locale before a portal can be deployed.

**Problem Statement:** How are translation units (TUs) authored, stored, translated, and resolved at runtime — and how does the architecture guarantee 100% locale coverage before deployment?
page_texts.6:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-I18N-002-medicaid-portal-localization.md#decision-drivers]

### Decision Drivers

- 📋 Compliance — Medicaid accessibility and language access requirements mandate Spanish support as a baseline
- ⚡ Performance — locale switch must be instantaneous; no server round-trip
- 🌐 Sustainability — MT + MTPE (machine translation with post-editing) scales to any number of locales
- 🔒 Translation integrity — human-reviewed translations (HTR) must never be overwritten by MT
- 🚫 Zero hard-coded strings — every user-visible string must go through the i18n layer

page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-I18N-002-medicaid-portal-localization.md#two-layer-i18n-architecture-with-bake-at-publish-and-mt-fill]

### Two-Layer i18n Architecture with Bake-at-Publish and MT Fill

**Description:** Studio UI uses `next-intl` static catalogs. Portal content TUs are compiled into Page Assembly artifacts at publish time. MT via the Gainwell AI Agentic Framework fills missing TUs in all target locales. All portals and Product Packages ship with `en-US` + `es-MX` by default.

**Layer 1 — Studio UI (build plane):**
- Library: `next-intl` (latest stable)
- Message catalog format: ICU MessageFormat strings in `components/studio/messages/{locale-code}.json`
- Locale negotiation: cookie-driven (`studio_locale`); fallback to `en-US`
- Default locales: `en-US` (source) and `es-MX`
- Loaded via static `import()` at build time — no runtime TMS dependency

**Layer 2 — Portal content (serve plane):**
- All TUs are baked into the Page Assembly artifact at publish time
- Portal runtime resolves TUs client-side from the pre-compiled artifact — zero server round-trips on locale switch
- Default locales: `en-US` (source, non-removable) and `es-MX` for every portal and Product Package
- 100% coverage gate: a page cannot be published if any TU in any registered target locale is missing
- MT fill: one-click MT action submits all missing/MT-provenance TUs to the Gainwell AI Agentic Framework; HTR strings are never overwritten
- BCP-47 locale tag support; no architectural limit on number of target locales

**No hard-coded strings invariant:** Every user-visible string — including field labels, validation messages, tooltips, button labels, placeholder text, HTML block content, IFrame accessible names, page title/banner/notice/error/footer regions, navigation item labels, persona display names, and persona descriptions — must be externalized as a translation unit. Components with hard-coded user-visible strings fail the component certification gate.

**Pros:**
- ✅ Locale switch is instantaneous — full multi-locale content is in the pre-loaded artifact
- ✅ MT provides 100% coverage baseline at near-zero marginal cost per new locale
- ✅ `en-US` + `es-MX` ship with every portal and Product Package by default
- ✅ HTR strings are protected from MT overwrites

**Cons:**
- ❌ Page Assembly payload grows with (TU count × locale count) — must monitor for large portals
- ❌ Adding a new target locale requires republishing all pages

---
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-I18N-002-medicaid-portal-localization.md#option-1-bake-at-publish-with-mt-fill-selected]

### Option 1: Bake-at-Publish with MT Fill (Selected)

**Description:** All TUs compiled into Page Assembly artifact at publish; MT fills missing TUs.

**Pros:**
- ✅ Zero round-trips on locale switch; MT scales to any number of locales

**Cons:**
- ❌ Payload grows with locale count
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-I18N-002-medicaid-portal-localization.md#option-2-server-side-string-resolution-per-request]

### Option 2: Server-Side String Resolution per Request

**Description:** Portal fetches translated strings from a TMS API on each page request.

**Pros:**
- ✅ Strings can be updated without republishing

**Cons:**
- ❌ Adds latency to every page request; TMS API becomes a critical runtime dependency; violates build/serve plane isolation (ADR-APP-001)
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-I18N-002-medicaid-portal-localization.md#option-3-lazy-locale-loading-fetch-on-locale-switch]

### Option 3: Lazy Locale Loading (fetch on locale switch)

**Description:** Only the active locale's strings are loaded; additional locales fetched on switch.

**Pros:**
- ✅ Reduces initial page payload

**Cons:**
- ❌ Locale switch causes a visible loading delay; TMS API dependency at runtime; more complex client-side state management

---
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-I18N-002-medicaid-portal-localization.md#decision-outcome]

## Decision Outcome

**Selected:** Option 1 — Bake-at-Publish with MT Fill.

Consistent with ADR-APP-001 (build/serve plane isolation): the serve plane reads only from prebuilt artifacts. No runtime TMS dependency. MT via the Gainwell AI Agentic Framework makes 100% coverage practical.

---
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-I18N-002-medicaid-portal-localization.md#-positive]

### ✅ Positive

- Locale switch is instantaneous for all end users
- MT makes 100% coverage feasible for any number of target locales without proportional translation effort
- `en-US` + `es-MX` are available in every portal out of the box
page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-I18N-002-medicaid-portal-localization.md#-negative]

### ❌ Negative

- Adding a new target locale requires a publish + deploy cycle to bake new TUs into the artifact
page_texts.17:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-I18N-002-medicaid-portal-localization.md#-neutral]

### ⚪ Neutral

- Studio UI locale and portal content locales are independent — no coupling required

---
page_texts.19:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-I18N-002-medicaid-portal-localization.md#-risks]

### ⚠️ Risks

- MT quality insufficient for regulated Medicaid content (safety notices, eligibility information)
- Page Assembly payload too large for portals with many TUs and many locales
page_texts.20:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-I18N-002-medicaid-portal-localization.md#-mitigations]

### 🛡️ Mitigations

- MTPE model: MT provides baseline coverage; HTR post-editing elevates critical strings. Human review before marking a string HTR
- Monitor artifact size; evaluate lazy locale loading if a portal exceeds 10 target locales

---
page_texts.21:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-I18N-002-medicaid-portal-localization.md#compliance-notes]

## Compliance Notes

- **Regulatory:** Language access requirements (e.g., Title VI, state Medicaid language access plans) mandate Spanish support. `es-MX` ships as a default locale for all portals.
- **Security:** No PHI flows through the translation pipeline. Translation units are UI strings only — never patient data.
- **Standards:** No conflicting i18n/l10n guidance found in `eap-ref-architecture`. This ADR establishes the project-level i18n pattern.

---

[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-I18N-002-medicaid-portal-localization.md#glossary]

## Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **TU** | Translation Unit — a single translatable string identified by a key |
| **MT** | Machine Translation — AI-generated translation |
| **HTR** | Human-Translated — reviewed and approved by a human translator |
| **MTPE** | Machine Translation with Post-Editing — MT draft reviewed by a human |
| **TMS** | Translation Management System — external tool for managing translation workflows (not used in this architecture) |
| **BCP-47** | IETF standard for locale tags (e.g., `en-US`, `es-MX`) |
| **Source locale** | The locale in which all content is originally authored (`en-US`) |
| **Target locale** | Any locale other than the source locale |
